note: Community firmwares for the M-VAVE FM-1: the FM-1 Firmware Hub's list (thefirmwarehub.com, tools/hub_catalog.mjs; its packages fetched from the Hub), then our own list (web/firmwares-own.json: this repository's FM-1 SID, M-VAVE's own, a few from fm1-editor.com/firmware). Generated: edit web/firmwares-own.json (the default too), not this file. The web page fetches each package when started and unpacks it with web/fwsc.js; tools/fetch_firmwares.mjs does the same into reference/firmwares for fm1-live. "hub": the firmware's id on the Hub (its card: thefirmwarehub.com/#fw-<hub>).

firmwares.name: M-VAVE stock firmware
firmwares.author: M-VAVE
firmwares.about: The firmware the FM-1 ships with: a DX7-style FM synth, both cores running. This page does not host it and cannot download it (M-VAVE's server does not allow other pages to): download FM-1.fwsc from M-VAVE, then open it here; this browser keeps it for next time. Its patches live in flash an update does not carry, so it starts with a small bank of the emulator's own; "DX7 bank…" loads a 32-voice .syx.

firmwares.name: Felucca
firmwares.author: hugelton
firmwares.about: The original open firmware: a four-operator FM synth with sequencer, arpeggiator and effects.

firmwares.name: Felucca [Salt]
firmwares.author: ChanceTheMaker
firmwares.about: A Felucca fork with its own sound and editor changes.

firmwares.name: 386DX
firmwares.author: seajaysec
firmwares.about: A karaoke robot with a band: it sings songs from karaoke and MIDI files, or lines you type, to the notes you play. Its face is the voice. Keys, bass and drums play along, with a step sequencer and sixteen punch-in effects.

firmwares.name: AMB-1
firmwares.author: charlesvestal
firmwares.about: A generative ambient machine inspired by Music for Airports.

firmwares.name: April OS
firmwares.author: beashoko
firmwares.license: MIT (its repository, which holds the installer page; the firmware source is not published)
firmwares.about: A sampler inspired by the Casio SK-1: no synth engines, only samples, recorded through the installer page's microphone bridge.

firmwares.name: BEETLE
firmwares.author: Joppe Sikken (SikkenWorks)
firmwares.about: A tracker for the FM-1: patterns written top to bottom, step by step, with note, instrument, chord and effect columns, the way trackers have always worked.

firmwares.name: Bunker Evolved
firmwares.author: Kid Bunka
firmwares.about: Generative ambient: four editable layers from 64 sound recipes, 24 worlds, 24 motifs and 32 scales. GROW varies the phrases, seven EVOLVE processes change them over time. Felucca's sound pages stay. Built on Felucca 1.6.1.

firmwares.name: Bytemania
firmwares.author: lloyd (llozd)
firmwares.about: A bytebeat synth: play one-line formulas, tweak them with the knobs, and write your own, with a random button in the formula creator that is really fun. A beta, built on Dinghy.

firmwares.name: Carnac OS
firmwares.author: OrbVorgis
firmwares.about: A dual-timbral wavetable synth after Carnac's standing stones: 15 morphing wavetable banks, seven voice architectures, a MAQ 16/3-style sequencer for modulated sequences and a chord sequencer for progressions, spring, tomb and tank reverbs. Its own installer also writes its wavetables. Built on X0X and Felucca.

firmwares.name: Chipbox
firmwares.author: Pasquale Barilla
firmwares.about: A chiptune groovebox with replicas of the NES, Game Boy and Sega Master System sound chips, in three views: RACK for the 16 steps of a page, CHIP to set up each channel, SONG to chain the pages into a song.

firmwares.name: ChoralRoot
firmwares.author: Quixotic7
firmwares.about: A port of the Choral Root synth.

firmwares.name: fm1-chord
firmwares.author: math0ne
firmwares.about: A chord machine after the HiChord, with extras: chords in a key under the white keys, slash chords and inversions, sounds, envelopes, effects and a looper.

firmwares.name: Clipper
firmwares.author: isod89
firmwares.about: A deep synth grown out of SLOOP: 23 engines and 407 sounds, from HYBRID (three oscillators, two filters, a mod matrix) to six-operator FM, wavetables, wave sequencing, a Juno and physical models; arp, step sequencer, MPE and a web editor for every parameter.

firmwares.name: CoralFlower
firmwares.author: FicusFicusov
firmwares.about: Chords after the Orchid, with a UX made for the FM-1: one key turns every note into a chord with a bass, 27 scales, an arpeggiator, a looper, a plate reverb, and a pixel flower that grows as you play.

firmwares.name: CS-1
firmwares.author: twochannels
firmwares.about: A Yamaha CS-80 in spirit: eight voices of two channels, high- and low-pass filters in series, ring modulator, the touch response and 22 tones from the owner's manual. A sound module played over MIDI.

firmwares.name: CTL-1
firmwares.author: charlesvestal
firmwares.about: A MIDI controller: the keys play in a scale with its chords on the black keys, four banks of knobs, an arpeggiator and Euclidean drums, with General MIDI sounds of its own.

firmwares.name: Cut-A-Dor
firmwares.author: Kid Bunka
firmwares.about: A beat dojo for scratch DJs and beatmakers: boom bap, lo-fi and breaks from 16 rhythm families with swing and fills, an eight-lane 32-step sequencer, punch-in effects you record bar by bar, a bass voice. Sound banks and editor in the browser.

firmwares.name: Del Rio
firmwares.author: Jess Del Rio
firmwares.about: A rhythm box of ceremony percussion: djembe, cajon, udu, clapsticks, maracas and triangle, their real strokes on the black keys, a step sequencer on the white keys and 31 rhythms from the literature. Played alone: a berimbau with its caxixi, a buzzing tanpura and a breathing shruti box. Built on fm1-base.

firmwares.name: Dinghy
firmwares.author: zvenson
firmwares.about: Your base for your own FM-1 firmware: everything under it done and documented (updates, USB rescue, USB-MIDI, USB audio, keys, screen, settings), a 4-voice sine on top. Fork it, replace the sine.

firmwares.name: DRIFT
firmwares.author: FBNFRTG
firmwares.about: An ambient instrument for live sessions: warm synths, spacious pads and delicate plucks over a generative Euclidean sequencer on one track, with delays and reverbs from spring to shimmer. Built on Felucca.

firmwares.name: DUB-1
firmwares.author: sbegueria
firmwares.about: A generative dub techno machine that plays itself from the moment it is on: chord stabs into a tape echo, FM pings, a sub bass on five grooves, a ducking kick, crackle, and an eight-bar arrangement with breaks and fills.

firmwares.name: DUELL
firmwares.author: OSCILL/R
firmwares.about: A multimorphing bitimbral synthesizer: two complete parts, three ways to play them together, and a morph that glides between two versions of every sound.

firmwares.name: Evander's Music Box
firmwares.author: Michail Tsakiroglou
firmwares.about: A bard's instrument for LARP, medieval and high fantasy: recorder, hurdy-gurdy, harp and a tavern kit on four tracks, encounters and songs for the table. "Mother Melody hears thy song."

firmwares.name: ETCH
firmwares.author: SikkenWorks
firmwares.about: Draw the sound: a waveform drawn and changed with the knobs, morphed into another one, and a third modulating the result. An experimental build.

firmwares.name: Fart Machine One
firmwares.author: adamcharleswilsonmusic-code
firmwares.about: A questionable musical instrument: eleven artisanal farts, reverb, delay and a sixteen-step sequencer.

firmwares.name: Felucca 8 Patterns
firmwares.author: echoe
firmwares.about: Felucca 1.5.1 with eight sequences a track to switch between and chain one after another; the user samples are left out to make room.

firmwares.name: FiMba-1
firmwares.author: jadamsowers
firmwares.about: A physically modelled kalimba (thumb piano), with mbira patterns, tape and grains. Built on Felucca, X0X and FoMni.

firmwares.name: Flyfish
firmwares.author: delirioux
firmwares.about: One piece on the FM-1: Chopin's Étude Op. 10 No. 1 on a sampled Steinway D. It plays the étude, lets you shape it with rubato, touch and accents, practise it and move it. Built on Tuna and Felucca.

firmwares.name: FM-106
firmwares.author: PatttF
firmwares.about: The Juno-106 emulation of KR-106 ported to the FM-1: six voices on both cores, the BBD stereo chorus, 128 factory presets and a 1980s Roland look.

firmwares.name: fm1-dock
firmwares.author: joakimeriksson
firmwares.about: One firmware, many synths: CS-1, Scintilla and OberVave as modules in flash, the sine built in; HOME opens the picker. Add FM-106, MONK-1, FiMba-1, GATOR, DUB-1, FM-1 SID, AMB-1 or FoMni from its page with one click; Bluetooth MIDI with both cores, a master EQ, MIDI options. Formerly harbor.

firmwares.name: FM-1 Doom
firmwares.author: zvenson
firmwares.about: Doom on the FM-1: one arena from FreeDM, played on the keys and a knob, on the FM-1's screen, with synthesised sound effects and no music.

firmwares.name: FM1-GM
firmwares.author: jartificer
firmwares.about: A General MIDI sequencer with 16 tracks, 128 General MIDI instruments to choose from and a drum kit (on track 10). It can store up to 64 songs, each containing up to 128 measures.

firmwares.name: FMEL-1
firmwares.author: Antonio Altea
firmwares.about: Mellotron-style tape sounds, coloured with effects and lo-fi tape: flutes, strings and choirs as on the old tape frames, played from the keys.

firmwares.name: FMini-1
firmwares.author: Ruppert
firmwares.about: A three-oscillator monosynth in the spirit of the classic Moogs: a 24 dB/octave ladder filter, two contours, 100 factory patches, an arpeggiator, a sequencer and MIDI. Built on Felucca.

firmwares.name: FOMAJAM
firmwares.author: konsumer
firmwares.about: A drum machine in the classic step-grid style: voices after the 909, 808, 707, 606, DMX and more, a machine per voice, accents and patterns. Play it in the browser first.

firmwares.name: FoMni
firmwares.author: charlesvestal
firmwares.about: A chord harp inspired by the Omnichord: hold a chord, strum the keys.

firmwares.name: FRASIL
firmwares.author: Styves Goupil
firmwares.about: An ambient drone and texture instrument: tap a key to latch a drone, a note or a chord in your key, press to swell it. Three layers a voice into a big reverb with shimmer and freeze; GLINT plays icy FM bells on top, by hand, by arpeggiator or a 32-step sequencer, and BASS holds a deep note below.

firmwares.name: Frodhes
firmwares.author: Leonardo Mirabal
firmwares.about: A Rhodes electric piano, physically modelled, no samples: four piano types, compressor, drive, tremolo or wah, phaser, chorus, delay and reverb, tap tempo, MIDI clock, scales and presets. Built on Dinghy.

firmwares.name: FuMi-1
firmwares.author: cartesive
firmwares.about: Inspired by the Suiko ST-50 shigin conductor: koto and shakuhachi-style tones.

firmwares.name: Pocket GammaWave
firmwares.author: ShadowTune (GammaWave Audio)
firmwares.about: The companion to the GammaWave desktop synth: four industrial distortions, vowel and scream filters, an FFT spectrogram, a four-track tape deck screen and a song generator with 49 genres, trap and drill too.

firmwares.name: GHOULBOX
firmwares.author: jasonpersinger
firmwares.about: Dungeon synth (a Felucca fork): cathedral reverb and dark drones.

firmwares.name: Golana
firmwares.author: Gadlele
firmwares.about: One analog-style synth laid out like the classic microKORG, with a screen that draws the sound.

firmwares.name: Golana DZ Edition
firmwares.author: dzwerg
firmwares.about: Golana's synth with a sequencer for whole songs: 64 steps a pattern, 32 programs (up to 2,048 steps), a SONGMODE that plays from a first to a last program once or on repeat, and USB MIDI out to sequence other synths.

firmwares.name: GR!MM
firmwares.author: GRiMMBIENT
firmwares.about: Dark ambient, dungeon synth and deathdream: four tracks, seven sound sources from VA and 6-op FM to formant voices and physical models, tape, granular freeze and reverbs up to infinite, a 64-step sequencer and song mode. Built on Dinghy.

firmwares.name: HERA
firmwares.author: Ben Badio
firmwares.about: A chord groovebox after the Roland J-6: 100 chord sets, 9 phrase styles with 12 variations each and a 64-pattern step sequencer, on a four-voice Juno-style synth from Clipper with chorus, delay and reverb. A chord map on the screen shows which chord sits on which key. Built on Dinghy.

firmwares.name: Hortator
firmwares.author: DeadActive
firmwares.about: A drum-focused firmware based on Felucca.

firmwares.name: HYP-1
firmwares.author: RedtailWorks
firmwares.about: Hypnotic techno and acid: a breathing pad, a deep drone, a generative 303 line and grain over drums you sequence. Flip patterns on the bar, break it down, build it up. Forked from AMB-1.

firmwares.name: Jangada
firmwares.author: zednaked
firmwares.about: Superwave analog voices and a modulation matrix.

firmwares.name: JIANT FM
firmwares.author: juanjiant-bit
firmwares.about: A bio-synthetic groovebox: six tracks drawn as living beings, eight engines (FM6 with Dexed, analog, phase, voice), mutating macros and SLOOP's song mode. Still in development.

firmwares.name: KAWA
firmwares.author: Omnipotard (Guizmoh)
firmwares.about: A pocket tracker for any style: six tracks with an engine each (pulse, 4-bit wave, noise, 6-operator FM, drum kit or sample), patterns chained into a song, 32 live effects and tools that write beats for you. A beta, not yet tried on a real FM-1 by its maker.

firmwares.name: Ketch
firmwares.author: risseraka
firmwares.about: A tracker in the LSDJ / picoTracker / M8 line: song, chain and phrase screens, instruments, effects and a mixer, on the FM-1's own keys and screen.

firmwares.name: LOOM-8
firmwares.author: Charles Vestal
firmwares.about: A groovebox inspired by the OP-XY: eight tracks on nine engines, step tricks and locks, weave, a conductor and throws.

firmwares.name: MAKU
firmwares.author: okumurari
firmwares.about: An ambience machine for DJ interludes: switch it on and a random world in key plays, four parts, buttons that are verbs, and the worlds you like breed new ones. Clock follow. Play it in the browser first.

firmwares.name: MC-1
firmwares.author: dspaudio
firmwares.about: An original four-part groovebox with a 1990s workflow: three melodic parts and a 16-lane drum part, 128 melodic presets, eight drum kits, song arrangement, an arpeggiator and recorded knob moves.

firmwares.name: Melodee
firmwares.author: keremimo
firmwares.about: Total playing pleasure, far beyond Felucca: recording without quantize, microtonal scales, a Casio CZ-1, a bit-by-bit Dexed, scale modes made for an MPC Sample as its companion.

firmwares.name: MIN-1
firmwares.author: Reytian
firmwares.about: A tiny minimalist ensemble after Philip Glass: it starts playing when you switch on, you join whenever you like. In EASY mode every white key is a chord that fits. Four models, twenty pieces.

firmwares.name: Mini-Tone
firmwares.author: Stéphane Schmitz
firmwares.about: Felucca with six tracks and new engines: SID, Braids' 48 models, a TB-303 and engines after Elektron's Analog Four, SY Chip and Digitone 2, a ping-pong delay and a new reverb. Built on Felucca 1.5.

firmwares.name: MODELAR
firmwares.author: Hirakos
firmwares.about: A semi-modular drone synth played like a Kaoss Pad: four oscillators modulating each other through eight routings, and keys that move a cursor on an XY pad instead of playing notes: white keys are points, black keys gestures. ARP, a polymetric sequencer, a clock in Hz and eight generative environments.

firmwares.name: MONK-1
firmwares.author: Charles Vestal
firmwares.about: Twelve singers, from Jerry the monk to Snider the punk, each in its own voice: MonkSynth's formant voices, played with velocity and pressure from the FM-1's own keys.

firmwares.name: MORPHEUS
firmwares.author: Ben Badio
firmwares.about: A pattern sequencer after Reason's Matrix: up to four channels of MIDI sequence data out, and a few voices built in to build the patterns with.

firmwares.name: Mutable Dreams
firmwares.author: Kid Bunka
firmwares.about: A generative instrument after a small modular setup: six interchangeable tracks on eight engines (selected Plaits algorithms, Rings' modal resonator, a Choir of its own), 64 Biomes, Euclidean rhythms with probability, four macros and a granular bus. Plays and edits in the browser.

firmwares.name: MYCELIUM
firmwares.author: Mandalars
firmwares.about: Forest, Psytrance, Goa and Hitech grooves, built on Felucca and SLOOP: original drums and icons and four factory songs. A test release: not yet fully tested on the device.

firmwares.name: Niagara Drift
firmwares.author: evanyerburgh
firmwares.about: A drone synth: two drifting virtual-analog drones, each with its own part, swells, LFOs, effects and a sequencer.

firmwares.name: No Man Sky FM
firmwares.author: Hericdk
firmwares.about: A space adventure while you make music, built on SLOOP 2.7.1: fly between planets with two knobs, land, mine, fight sentinels and warp between stars, every SLOOP screen floating over the game.

firmwares.name: NOIZ DEMONS
firmwares.author: SPIKE the Percussionist
firmwares.about: Felucca with randomization as a ritual: every new sound summons one of 30 demons of the Ars Goetia, its sigil takes the screen and its rank decides how wild the sound gets.

firmwares.name: OberVave
firmwares.author: zvenson
firmwares.about: An 8-voice analog-style poly in the spirit of the classic American polys of 1979-84: two oscillators a voice, sync, cross-mod, a 12 / 24 dB filter with a SEM-style morph, an arpeggiator with hold, chorus, ping-pong delay and a plate reverb. A two-track step sequencer played as sloopDX: live recording on top, chords, long notes, a click and a count-in.

firmwares.name: OPN-1
firmwares.author: putchdev
firmwares.about: The Sega Genesis / Mega Drive's Yamaha YM2612: six channels of 4-operator FM. Its web app takes patches from game music (VGM) and OPM files and streams VGM tunes to the FM-1 to play.

firmwares.name: ORBIT
firmwares.author: dspaudio
firmwares.about: A four-track groovebox based on SLOOP: three synth parts and a drum machine, an event tape to rearrange them, OP-1-inspired screens.

firmwares.name: PIGEON
firmwares.author: The Shrimp Blimp
firmwares.about: An old-school hip-hop and house sampler after the SP-404 and the PO-33: two song samples and a 16-pad kit, up to 32 chops a song, a 64-step sequencer, patterns and a song arrangement. Built on Felucca.

firmwares.name: Polly
firmwares.author: charlesvestal
firmwares.about: A pocket arranger after the Yamaha QY70: pick a style, play a chord and a band of eight follows, with General MIDI sounds.

firmwares.name: PurpleMonkey
firmwares.author: Quixotic7
firmwares.about: A firmware for kids.

firmwares.name: FM1 Quest
firmwares.author: hericdk
firmwares.about: A live RPG adventure inside the synth.

firmwares.name: Rainbow Mode
firmwares.author: joshbartlettband-web
firmwares.about: A music toy for little hands (a Felucca fork).

firmwares.name: Shine On
firmwares.author: zvenson
firmwares.about: A string ensemble in the spirit of the late-70s machines, grown out of OberVave: divide-down keyers with 16', 8' and 4' footages, register filters, a three-tap BBD ensemble and a phaser, on two tracks with the sequencer.

firmwares.name: FM-1 SID
firmwares.author: joakimeriksson
firmwares.about: A SID chip on the FM-1, its own firmware on fm1-dock (fm1-dock's USB, installer and rescue; the sine as the fallback): a C64 tune player (reSID 0.16 and a 6510 running the tune's own code, PSID and RSID) starting with GoatTracker 2's example songs, Dojo first; a GoatTracker editor; and a synth: the keys play 12 instruments, KNOB1-4 are cutoff, resonance, attack, release; FX opens chorus, delay and reverb. Its page plays all of HVSC and sends any .sid to a real FM-1 over USB (Play on my FM-1), and the FM-1's keys play the page. Installed and playing on a real FM-1: joakimeriksson.github.io/fm1-emu/fm1-sid/

firmwares.name: SID-1
firmwares.author: putchdev
firmwares.about: The Commodore 64's SID chip, twice for six voices. Its web app edits patches and takes them straight from .sid game music files.

firmwares.name: SIDOU
firmwares.author: Denis Sablić
firmwares.about: Turns the FM-1 into a C64 SID machine: two SIDs (6581 and 8580) with the chip's character dialled in, a GoatTracker 2 compatible tracker and step sequencer, and a live instrument to play over a song.

firmwares.name: Skiff
firmwares.author: illuminus5
firmwares.about: A six-track groovebox built on Felucca 1.1.5: fourteen synth and drum engines, a 64-step sequencer with chords, ratchets and locks, songs and a performance layer.

firmwares.name: SLOOP
firmwares.author: isod89
firmwares.about: A live groovebox: four looping tracks.

firmwares.name: SLOOP ALG
firmwares.author: shaw-core
firmwares.about: A SLOOP test build with extra FM algorithms.

firmwares.name: SLOOP DX7 Banks
firmwares.author: majnikool
firmwares.about: SLOOP with up to twelve DX7 voice banks and presets grouped by kind. Test builds.

firmwares.name: SLOOP Floyd FM
firmwares.author: renebohne
firmwares.about: SLOOP with a four-operator FM engine after Floyd Steinberg's 4-OP idea: an envelope per operator and a live oscilloscope that draws the envelopes as you play.

firmwares.name: sloopDX
firmwares.author: zvenson
firmwares.about: SLOOP's live workflow with a six-operator DX7 engine from Dexed: 32 algorithms, your own .syx banks, every voice edited on the FM-1, and FM drums.

firmwares.name: Tessera
firmwares.author: Theo Dainis (Rastapopolix)
firmwares.about: Generative music on four tracks: each plays its own steps, an arpeggio or one of 13 generators (Turing, Euclid, Markov, Constellation, Chord and more), and the tracks evolve, follow and modulate each other. EVOLVE and FORM grow phrases into songs; 16 mod cords connect anything. A Melodee fork.

firmwares.name: Tonitor
firmwares.author: Nuno Zimas
firmwares.about: Six tracks for live ambient and experimental music: three synth engines, patches generated by algorithm, free-length loops with up to ten overdubs each, a granulator, filters and a lush reverb.

firmwares.name: TRIBE
firmwares.author: apiel
firmwares.about: A ten-track groovebox built on X0X where any engine plays on any track: kicks, 909 and 808 voices, a 303, sixteen clips a track and scatter effects.

firmwares.name: Tuna
firmwares.author: delirioux
firmwares.about: Generative music built on Felucca: composer profiles write the music as it plays, you steer them. A work in progress.

firmwares.name: Unholy Union
firmwares.author: actuallysparky
firmwares.about: Generative ambient and drone: Immaculate Permutation rolls an arrangement in one key, a pad, a sequence and a chord arpeggio under a fourth voice for your hands. Keep a sermon you like, evolve it, or reveal another.

firmwares.name: Vector37
firmwares.author: genkigenki
firmwares.about: An orbiting overtone synth: four corners of two overtone generators each, a sun on a path and a moon around it decide how much of each you hear; the knobs shape the selected planet. Made for the SMK-37, here its FM-1 build. After the Beetlecrab Vector.

firmwares.name: WaveLoop FM-1
firmwares.author: ELI7VH
firmwares.about: A Felucca mod: standalone Arturia MiniLab 3 control, fine track mixing, a DJ filter, momentary effects and MIDI feedback.

firmwares.name: winampFM Synth
firmwares.author: hericdk
firmwares.about: Winamp 2.x on the FM-1, built on SLOOP: your sounds as a playlist, four tracks recorded as loops, effects on sliders and a visualizer of lines.

firmwares.name: X0X
firmwares.author: charlesvestal
firmwares.about: A groovebox: 909, 808, two 303s and a break player. Pick a drum with a black key, set steps with the white keys, then PLAY.

firmwares.name: X0X-RMX
firmwares.author: Mr-Roboto (Oliver)
firmwares.about: X0X remixed after The Orb: banks and patterns reordered live per voice, Grids MAP and EUCLID drum generation, an extended TB-3PO with 22 scales and a morphing 303 waveform. Built on X0X.

firmwares.name: ZEN-1
firmwares.author: aceyprime
firmwares.about: Ambient as a living window: cherry petals on a river, koi in a pond, fireflies under a real moon, and every movement a note. Set it down and let it play; the keys play along, the knobs shape the scene.

firmwares.name: zp12
firmwares.author: zvenson
firmwares.about: A 12-bit sampling drum machine after the E-mu SP-1200: 32 pads at 26 kHz with no interpolation, filtered channels on the knobs, loops and songs.
